title: How a Car Gearbox Works in 60 Seconds ⚙️🚗 #shorts
description:
An engine alone can't pull a car from a standstill. A manual gearbox uses a clutch, a layshaft and pairs of gears, and a synchromesh locks the chosen gear to the output shaft, trading speed for pulling power. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#gearbox #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: The Secret
steps.text: An engine spins fast but weak. Gears trade that *speed* for pulling power.

steps.label: Clutch
steps.text: First, the *clutch* disconnects the engine so you can change gear.

steps.label: Layshaft
steps.text: The engine drives the input shaft, which turns a *layshaft* full of gears.

steps.label: Free Gears
steps.text: Those gears turn matching gears on the *main shaft*, but they spin freely.

steps.label: Locking In
steps.text: Move the stick and a *synchromesh* collar slides over, locking one gear to the shaft.

steps.label: First vs Top
steps.text: A small gear driving a big one gives *high torque* for starting. Higher gears trade it for speed.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Gears trade speed for *torque*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
